features.name: Use Case Templates
features.does: Provides battle-tested conversational starters and prompt patterns for open-ended assistants and structured data collection.
features.value: Gets teams from an initial idea to a talking voice agent in seconds rather than starting from blank prompts.
features.say: Pre-built templates let you launch tested reception or support flows immediately. Your team starts from proven patterns instead of building from a blank slate.
features.ask: When a customer calls your front desk today, what are the top two or three things they are trying to get done?
features.limits: Templates initialize baseline prompts; custom organizational policies require further instruction tuning.
features.ask_technical: What conversational flow or agent role are you looking to scaffold first using pre-built base templates?

features.name: Conversation Type Selection
features.does: Switches the agent's core interaction model between open dialogue and schema-enforced field extraction that automatically terminates on completion.
features.value: Guarantees structured transactional records for business workflows without relying on unpredictable prompt adherence.
features.say: Choose whether the agent has a natural open conversation or systematically collects required intake details. This ensures your systems get complete, accurate customer information every time.
features.ask: Are your staff mostly answering open questions, or are they taking down specific details like names, dates, and account numbers?
features.limits: Data collection automatically ends the call when all required fields are collected.
features.ask_technical: Do you need open-ended multi-turn dialog or a schema-guided data collection agent that emits structured JSON payloads?

features.name: Conversation Instructions & Variables
features.does: Accepts natural language system prompts governing persona, tone, guardrails, and dynamic metadata variable interpolation (such as caller name).
features.value: Allows rapid prompt iteration with personalized context injected directly from CRM or SIP telephony metadata.
features.say: Clear guardrails keep the assistant firmly within your company policies while personalizing each call with caller data. It protects your brand while handling routine conversations automatically.
features.ask: What is the number one mistake a new hire might make on the phone that you would never want this assistant to repeat?
features.limits: A single prompt cannot replace complex multi-agent state machines, which require the LiveKit Python SDK.
features.ask_technical: What core system prompt guardrails, dynamic runtime variables, and persona constraints must be injected into the session?

features.name: Welcome Message & Interruption Handling
labels: Allow users to interrupt the greeting.
features.does: Defines the agent's initial spoken greeting upon joining, with native support for full barge-in interruption.
features.value: Establishes immediate human-grade conversational naturalness so callers can interrupt greetings without awkward waiting.
features.say: Callers can speak right over the opening greeting just like talking to a real person. This eliminates awkward pauses and stops callers from hanging up out of frustration.
features.ask: When someone calls in, do they usually want to cut right to the chase, or do they wait for a full greeting to finish?
features.limits: Overly broad welcome instructions can lead to rambling greetings; keep opening prompts to a greeting and a single question.
features.ask_technical: What initial greeting latency and barge-in interruption sensitivity do your callers require?

features.name: Call Ending & Webhook Delivery
features.does: Configures call completion logic, room teardown rules, post-call AI summarization, and webhook endpoints for extracted data delivery.
features.value: Closes the loop between voice conversations and enterprise backends by delivering structured summaries and payloads automatically.
features.say: Every call automatically logs clean summaries and collected data right into your existing business systems. Your staff gets actionable records without spending hours writing manual call notes.
features.ask: Once a call wraps up, who on your team needs to know what happened, and where does that record usually go?
use_cases: Automatic room deletion upon intake completion
features.limits: Data collection requires a valid endpoint URL to save call ending settings.
features.ask_technical: Which webhook endpoints or event queues should receive the structured call transcript and end-of-call summary?

features.name: Pipeline Mode Selection
features.does: Toggles between a modular STT-LLM-TTS processing pipeline and end-to-end multimodal speech-to-speech architectures.
features.value: Provides architectural flexibility to choose between swappable modular providers or cutting-edge unified realtime inference.
features.say: You can pick the underlying architecture that fits your exact latency and cost goals. That means you get human-like conversational speed without compromising on flexibility.
features.ask: Is your priority having the fastest possible response time so it feels like a real human, or having total flexibility over which AI vendors you use?
features.limits: Advanced client-side multimodal vision and complex tooling flows require the Python SDK.
features.ask_technical: Are you targeting modular STT-LLM-TTS orchestration or an integrated speech-to-speech realtime model architecture?

features.name: Text-to-Speech (TTS) & Expressive Mode
features.does: Configures vocal synthesis provider, voice identity, custom cloned voices, and emotional prosody through Expressive mode.
features.value: Delivers human-like voice quality tailored to company branding with sub-100ms streaming audio generation.
features.say: Expressive voices adapt their pacing and tone so conversations sound genuinely human and warm. Callers stay engaged and feel heard instead of trapped in a robotic phone menu.
features.ask: How important is it that your callers feel like they are speaking to a warm, empathetic person rather than an automated phone tree?
use_cases: Brand voice consistency across customer touchpoints
Empathetic tone for healthcare and support calls
features.limits: Custom voice cloning requires pre-uploading voice assets in the project Voices tab.
features.ask_technical: What TTS provider, neural voice clone, and expressive prosody settings are required for your target latency envelope?

features.name: Large Language Model (LLM) Selection
features.does: Selects the underlying reasoning model from leading open-source and proprietary models routed via LiveKit Inference.
features.value: Eliminates multiple vendor contracts and API keys while allowing instant model swaps without rewriting code.
features.say: Switch between leading AI models with a single click to balance intelligence against response speed. You always get the right level of reasoning for your specific budget and workflow.
features.ask: Do your calls require deep reasoning to solve tricky customer problems, or simple, lightning-fast answers to routine questions?
use_cases: High-speed conversational triage with lightweight models
features.limits: Builder uses unified Inference credits; custom self-hosted LLM endpoints require SDK deployment.
features.ask_technical: Which LLM model family and parameter size are you benchmarking for inference latency and task complexity?

features.name: Speech-to-Text (STT) & Keyterms
features.does: Configures speech transcription provider, language, and keyterm boosting for specialized domain vocabulary.
features.value: Ensures near-zero transcription error rates for brand names, drug nomenclature, and complex alphanumeric IDs.
features.say: Custom keyword recognition trains the system on your unique product names, industry jargon, and accents. This keeps callers from having to repeat themselves over simple misunderstandings.
features.ask: What industry terms, doctor names, or product codes do automated systems or new staff frequently mishear?
use_cases: Catalog SKU and product name recognition
features.limits: Custom keyterm lists are optimized for short phrases and specific vocabulary rather than paragraph prompts.
features.ask_technical: What specialized vocabulary, medical or domain acronyms, and phonetic keyterms need biasing in the transcription model?

features.name: Noise Cancellation & Background Audio
features.does: Provides server-side audio processing including machine-learning noise suppression (Quail) and ambient background audio simulation.
features.value: Isolates caller speech from noisy environments like cars or crowded rooms to maintain high transcription accuracy.
features.say: Built-in noise suppression filters out traffic, dogs, and background chatter before processing the caller's voice. The assistant understands callers clearly, even on noisy speakerphones.
features.ask: Are your callers often on speakerphone, in busy parking lots, or calling from noisy living rooms?
features.limits: Heavy acoustic echo requires caller-side hardware echo cancellation or headphones during testing.
features.ask_technical: What ambient noise suppression and telephony audio pre-processing thresholds are required before transcription?

features.name: HTTP Tools & Client Actions
features.does: Configures external REST API endpoints and client-side RPC functions that the agent triggers autonomously via LLM tool calls.
features.value: Transforms the voice agent from a passive conversationalist into an active system capable of executing transactions live.
features.say: The assistant can securely look up appointments, check account statuses, and update records during the call. That resolves customer requests end-to-end without pulling in your staff.
features.ask: What customer lookups or calendar checks do your staff spend the most time clicking through while on the phone?
use_cases: Live calendar availability lookup and appointment booking
Order status checks and tracking lookups
features.limits: Multi-step transactional rollbacks or complex conditional branching are best implemented in Python code.
features.ask_technical: What external REST endpoints or client-side tool definitions should the agent trigger during runtime execution?

features.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
features.does: Connects the agent directly to MCP servers over streaming HTTP/SSE, auto-discovering tools and resources dynamically.
features.value: Leverages the emerging MCP ecosystem to plug agents into enterprise data sources and third-party tools instantly.
features.say: Standardized tool connections let your voice assistant tap directly into your company tools. You expand what the assistant can do without rewriting custom integrations every time.
features.ask: Do you already have shared internal systems or business apps that all your customer tools need to connect to?
use_cases: Enterprise knowledge base retrieval via MCP
Developer tool execution and incident response
features.limits: Requires an accessible MCP server endpoint supporting SSE or HTTP streaming.
features.ask_technical: Do you plan to leverage Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to expose enterprise toolsets dynamically to the agent?

features.name: Agent Name & Identity
features.does: Establishes the unique system identifier used by LiveKit Cloud for explicit agent dispatch and SIP telephony routing.
features.value: Enables deterministic routing so phone numbers and frontend applications connect to the exact intended agent version.
features.say: Organized assistant identities make sure callers are immediately routed to the right specialist. It keeps call flows orderly across all your phone numbers and departments.
features.ask: If a caller dials your main number versus a direct line, should they reach the same assistant or different specialists?
features.limits: Renaming a deployed agent breaks existing SIP dispatch rules and frontend connection handles.
features.ask_technical: How will your inbound SIP dispatch rules map telephony numbers and client metadata to distinct agent dispatch names?

features.name: Custom Metadata & Environment Secrets
features.does: Manages mock test variables for prompt interpolation and securely stores encrypted API keys and auth headers.
features.value: Safeguards sensitive backend credentials while enabling realistic testing with caller-specific metadata.
features.say: Your private system keys and sensitive credentials stay fully encrypted in secure cloud storage. You can safely connect customer tools without exposing protected information.
features.ask: What sensitive customer information or internal system passwords need to be kept strictly protected during these calls?
use_cases: Mocking caller IDs and account numbers during preview
features.limits: Secrets are encrypted at rest; values cannot be read back once saved.
features.ask_technical: How are you managing encrypted runtime environment secrets and dynamic caller metadata payloads?

features.name: Telephony Dispatch & Phone Number Routing
features.does: Links agents directly to LiveKit Telephony SIP trunks and inbound dispatch rules for PSTN calling.
features.value: Provides a direct bridge from visual agent design to public phone numbers without third-party PBX middleware.
features.say: Attach this assistant directly to your existing business phone numbers or website with zero disruption. Callers get immediate help without your team needing to overhaul phone carriers.
features.ask: How do your customers reach you today—on existing office phone lines, a toll-free number, or through your website?
features.limits: Renting a live phone number incurs recurring telecom carrier fees and should not be executed during demos.
features.ask_technical: Are you provisioning new inbound phone numbers or interconnecting existing SIP trunks with WebRTC dispatch?

features.name: Live Interactive In-Browser Preview & Events Drawer
features.does: Runs an immediate live WebRTC voice session in the browser with audio waveforms, event streaming, and raw execution logs.
features.value: Shrinks prompt and behavior iteration loops to zero seconds by testing without packaging or deploying containers.
features.say: Test your assistant right in your browser microphone and see exactly how it reacts before going live. Your team can refine phrasing in seconds without waiting on technical deployments.
features.ask: How does your team currently check if a new phone script or greeting works before trying it out on real customers?
use_cases: Live verification of tool calling arguments
features.limits: Preview calls consume Inference tokens but are not saved to long-term Agent Insights session analytics.
features.ask_technical: How do prompt engineers and QA test conversation turns, tool executions, and event logs prior to release?

features.name: Live Realtime Python Code Generation
features.does: Translates visual builder settings into production-grade Python code utilizing the open-source LiveKit Agents framework.
features.value: Eliminates low-code lock-in by providing a transparent bridge from visual prototyping to developer git repos.
features.say: Every screen setting generates standard, exportable code that your developers fully own. You get the speed of a visual builder without ever being locked into a proprietary platform.
features.ask: Have you ever been stuck with software where you couldn't change how it worked because the vendor locked you out of the code?
use_cases: Smooth handoff from product prototyping to software engineering
Learning production LiveKit agent design patterns
Exporting to Git repositories for CI/CD deployments
features.limits: Changes made directly to downloaded Python code cannot be reverse-imported back into visual Agent Builder.
features.ask_technical: Do your software engineers require direct access to idiomatic, exportable Python code using the underlying SDK?

features.name: Cloud Container Deployment
features.does: Packages the agent into an optimized container and deploys it across LiveKit Cloud's globally distributed real-time infrastructure.
features.value: Provides one-click zero-DevOps production hosting with rolling zero-downtime updates and automated scaling.
features.say: One-click deployment automatically scales up during your busiest call spikes so no customer gets a busy signal. You never have to purchase or manage phone servers.
features.ask: What happens to your phone lines when call volume spikes on your busiest Monday morning of the month?
use_cases: Staging environments for client acceptance testing
Instant rollout of updated prompt versions
features.limits: Free tier permits one active deployed agent; higher concurrency requires standard Cloud tiers.
features.ask_technical: How do you handle container orchestration, autoscaling, and zero-downtime rolling deploys for voice workers?

features.name: Production Verification in Agent Console
features.does: Launches the LiveKit Agent Console to test the deployed production agent with end-to-end telemetry and latency waterfalls.
features.value: Enables rigorous verification of the live deployed instance across WebRTC media, model inference, and tool execution.
features.say: Real-time call inspection lets you trace every second of a conversation to pinpoint why an issue happened. You can quickly fix problems and maintain high service standards.
features.ask: When a caller has a bad phone experience, how do you currently figure out where things went wrong?
use_cases: Live latency breakdown across STT, LLM, and TTS
Production agent sanity testing before DNS/SIP cutover
Real-time event and tool execution validation
features.limits: Test in Console connects to the deployed cloud container, requiring a completed deployment build.
features.ask_technical: What observability and latency waterfall tooling do you use to diagnose per-turn response delays in production?

demo_instructions:
1. Start on the LiveKit Agents dashboard (/agents): point out high-level metrics (TOTAL SESSIONS, AVG LLM TOKENS / SESSION, INTERRUPTED RATE).
2. Explain that getting started with voice AI historically required stitching speech, intelligence, and audio streaming tools from scratch.
3. Click 'Deploy new agent' (top right x1259) to open the deployment menu.
4. Click 'Create in browser using Agent Builder' to open the template dialog, highlighting that this is a zero-setup visual workflow.
5. Select the 'Receptionist' template card under OPEN ENDED CONVERSATION, explaining that templates provide pre-tuned conversational baselines.
6. Ask discovery question: 'Where is your team spending the most time today: handling calls manually, setting up software, or trying to fix existing phone tools? (if technical: Where are you today: building, hosting, operating, or improving?)'
7. Scroll inside the dialog and click 'Create' (bottom right) to enter the Agent Builder on the 'Conversation' tab.
8. Point out the 'Open ended' and 'Data collection' options: explain that Data collection gathers specific required details like names and account numbers and sends them straight to your records (if technical: extracts structured schemas and POSTs JSON to a backend).
9. In the 'Instructions' textarea, highlight the persona and ask: 'What is the number one thing this assistant should never say or do with a customer? (if technical: What is the single most critical guardrail this agent must never violate?)'
10. Add their guardrail live into the Instructions prompt (e.g. 'Never quote specific pricing; always offer a representative').
11. Point out the 'Welcome message' card: verify it is toggled ON and that 'Allow users to interrupt the greeting.' is enabled so callers can speak right away without waiting out a recording.
12. Switch to the 'Models & Voice' tab: show the modular approach and all-in-one conversational options (if technical: 'STT-LLM-TTS pipeline' and 'Realtime model' options).
13. Point out 'Cartesia Sonic 3' under TTS, explain 'Expressive mode' for natural human cadence, and highlight 'Gemma 4 31B' under LLM.
14. Ask discovery question: 'How natural and responsive does this voice need to sound to keep your callers comfortable? (if technical: Which model providers and vocal latency targets are you standardized on?)'
15. Scroll down to show 'Speech-to-text (STT)', 'Keyterm recognition' for company product names and terms, and 'Noise cancellation'.
16. Switch to the 'Actions' tab: click 'Add HTTP tool' to demonstrate how the assistant looks up records or updates your system live on a call.
17. Mock the tool creation safely: explain how data passes between systems, and click 'Cancel' to avoid creating unauthenticated demo endpoints.
18. Switch to the 'Advanced' tab: highlight 'Agent name' (used to send calls to the right team), dynamic caller details, stored passwords, and incoming call routing.
19. Pitfall warning: point out 'Rent a number' under Telephony to explain phone routing, but never click to commit paid carrier rentals.
20. Switch the right panel to 'Code' (x1138): emphasize that every setting has compiled into clean, accessible code your team owns without vendor lock-in.
21. Switch back to 'Live preview' (x854) and click 'START CALL': grant microphone access and speak naturally with the agent.
22. Test the guardrail live by asking a forbidden pricing question, demonstrating immediate compliance and smooth interruption.
23. Point out the bottom drawer tabs (Audio, Events, Logs) to show live voice detection and activity tracking as you speak.
24. Click 'Deploy agent' (top right x1289) to package and launch the assistant with automatic capacity scaling so calls never drop.
25. Conclude by clicking 'Test in Console' (x1150) to demonstrate live call verification, timing breakdowns, and operational visibility.
presenter_notes: Find out what their agent should handle (e.g. booking appointments, answering patient questions) unless they already said. Create their agent with do_task, e.g. do_task("create an agent from the Appointment scheduling template named bright-smiles-front-desk"), picking the template that fits their use case. When the builder is open, name the tabs (Conversation, Models & Voice, Actions, Advanced), then go where they want. Explain what's on screen and why it matters for their business, and now and then ask that feature's question. When they want to try their agent: do_task("start a test call in the live preview"). When they ask for a change (switch the voice, edit the instructions, change the model), use act per click or field, e.g. "click the Models & Voice tab", "type <text> into the Instructions field".
